newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down slightly as units return.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down slightly as units return.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open slightly lower Monday on forecasts of near-normal temperatures in the U.S. West and the resumption of service from Western power generation units, industry sources said.

In early over the counter discussion, July Palo Verde (PV) was assessed at $27.65-28.00 with reports of a trade at $27.75 per megawatt hour (MWh), although the trade was not confirmed, the sources said.
July NYMEX PV settled Friday at $27.92 per MWh.
Also over the counter, July California Oregon Border (COB) was talked at $17.10-17.40 with reports of a trade at $17.30, although the trade was not confirmed.
NYMEX July COB closed last week at $17.42 per MWh.

In the West, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 on the coast of central California and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 near Phoenix, Arizona, were operating at full power early Monday after recent outages.
The 1,221 MW Palo Verde unit 2 was reduced to 86 percent of capacity as of early Monday to repair a main feedwater heater leak, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
Other generation units were also expected to return to service as utilities ended spring maintenance and refueling outages in preparation for summer service.

On Friday, the electricity futures settled lower in choppy trading as bearish sentiment overtook the market. The power complex suffered sharp losses early in the week on concerns over rising generation and easing air-conditioning demand in the Southwest.

Weather forecasts called for near normal temperatures through much of the week in the Southwest with little precipation expected. Temperatures were expected to fall to just below normal late in the week.
In Phoenix, Ariz., the maximum temperature was expected to reach 102 degrees Fahrenheit Tuesday with an overnight low tonight expected near 74 degrees.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average near normal then fall to a few degrees cooler than normal by the end of the week. Above-normal rainfall was expected through much of the area through the week.
NYMEX July Henry Hub natural gas futures opened down 1.8 cents at $2.17 per million British thermal units on Monday.
